title: human as a (non-agent) role: inline status-bar self-write + async-no-pause comprehension
method: Fresh sonnet agent given ONLY the modified instruction text (instructions.md inline-mode block + ralph-loop-overview inline block + composed CLAUDE.md async-no-pause section). No prior context. Answers must come from the supplied text alone.

questions.q: You are an agent and a human just sent you a direct (inline) message. What, specifically, should you do with the status-bar current-event indicator at the start of that turn, and why is it you (not a cycle wrapper) doing it?
questions.expected: Self-write the current-event indicator to `inline` (e.g. `cycle.py status-bar-self inline ""`). You do it because the cycle wrappers (cycle_pre/cycle_post) do NOT fire during an inline turn, so nothing else updates the bar.
questions.anti: Saying the wrapper/harness sets it, or that the bar is left stale/untouched.

questions.q: When does the `inline` status-bar value get cleared, and to what?
questions.expected: Cleared back to the agent's normal idle/working state when the inline session ends — the human signals done, or the next autonomous wake fires.
questions.anti: Saying it persists, or that the human/harness clears it.

questions.q: Does the older #9358 'treat a stale current-state bar as expected during inline mode' guidance still govern? Explain what replaced it.
questions.expected: No — it is superseded. The bar is no longer stale during inline mode; the agent self-writes an explicit `inline` value, so PM's sentinel reads an explicit state instead of tolerating staleness.
questions.anti: Saying #9358 still applies / the sentinel should still treat the bar as stale.

questions.q: You need a human decision mid-task and you are NOT in an inline session (you're in autonomous loop/event mode). What do you do — wait for the human, or something else? Be specific about the mechanism.
questions.expected: Do NOT wait. Assign a tracked ticket to the `human` alias (set role:<human> + the appropriate pending-human-* status) via a transition (not a bare comment), then immediately continue — pick up your next queue item or go idle. The human answers asynchronously.
questions.anti: Saying you pause/block/sit and wait for the human, or that you leave a bare comment.

questions.q: After you have assigned a 'need human' ticket to the human alias, how does the answer come back and who makes the forge transition to resume the work?
questions.expected: The return path is agent-mediated — a human never makes the forge transition. If the human reaches you (inline), you record the answer and re-assign the ticket back to yourself; if they reach PM, PM records it and re-assigns it to you on your behalf.
questions.anti: Saying the human makes the transition themselves, or that the ticket auto-routes back with no agent action.
